tests.cheap_to_run: Yes: CI runs `pnpm test` on Node 22/24/26 x ubuntu/windows with only a mock git user configured; e2e publish tests use a local test registry (@pnpm/pnpr), no credentials or paid services; the only CI secret is an optional Codecov upload token. Known Windows flakes are worked around in-repo, so Linux/macOS runs are the safe path.

verified.size_fit: 66 markdown docs excluding changelogs/.changeset files — comfortably in the 20-150 band. Repo is small (~426 checked-out files, 21 small packages), well clear of kubernetes-scale but substantive enough not to be a toy.
verified.summary: Strong fit. Genuinely load-bearing prose (semver/bump policy in docs/decisions.md, a publish-flow state-machine spec in packages/cli/src/commands/publish/README.md, an empirical package-manager behavior matrix in wiki/), a real 21-package pnpm monorepo, ~242 non-bot merged PRs in 18 months with ~60% in the 30-400 line band, a credential-free vitest suite with a local-registry e2e harness, MIT license, and 66 docs files. Docked two points for the docs/ vs site/ duplication (docs/ is banner-marked outdated, so an agent must know site/ is canonical), thin per-package READMEs, and heavy 2025 refactoring churn that may complicate replaying older PRs.

monorepo.evidence: Root package.json declares yarn workspaces ['packages/*', 'plugins/*']: 71 packages/ + 159 plugins/ = 230 workspace packages, plus a separate workspaces/ui tree. Nearly every plugin/package has its own README (560 non-changelog md in plugins/, 268 in packages/), so per-package docs are pervasive.

doc_dirs: docs/ (architecture-decisions, backend-system, frontend-system, conf, auth, integrations, features, tooling, permissions)
docs.evidence: docs/architecture-decisions/adr011-plugin-package-structure.md prescribes the x/x-backend/x-react/x-node/x-common package naming and placement convention (plugins/ vs packages/ reservation) — pure policy, not recoverable from source. docs/conf/defining.md defines the configSchema semantics: JSON-Schema-superset stitching across all @backstage-namespace dependencies, config.d.ts Config-type entry points, and @visibility/@items.visibility annotations controlling frontend exposure — semantics that live only in this prose. STYLE.md carries binding conventions (no null, no I-prefix, errors via @backstage/errors name-comparison, private constructors + static factories) enforced by review, not tooling. The 475 figure is curated prose (docs/ excluding the 285 release notes, plus beps/, contrib/, root files); total md excluding node_modules is ~1,891.

pr_history.suitability: Excellent volume and shape: of 30 sampled recent merges, well over a third land in the 30-400 changed-line band (e.g. #35020 139+/5-, #34618 114+/91-, #34996 273+/202-, #34873 306+/4-, #34816 71+/1-, #34904 63+/4-) with descriptive branch names, mandatory changeset summaries, and GitHub PR descriptions/linked issues; some renovate/dependabot noise to filter. Merge-commit bodies carry only PR titles, so descriptions must be fetched from GitHub per PR number.
pr_history.evidence: git log since 2025-02-01: 3,398 'Merge pull request #' merge commits + 262 '(#NNNN)' squash suffixes out of 12,771 total commits (~200 merged PRs/month).

tests.runner: Jest via 'backstage-cli repo test' (yarn test); Playwright for e2e
tests.cheap_to_run: Yes in money terms: no credentials or paid services; DB-backed tests fall back to in-memory/SQLite when BACKSTAGE_TEST_DATABASE_* connection strings are unset, CI sets BACKSTAGE_TEST_DISABLE_DOCKER=1, and services are mocked with MSW (ADR007). Obstacle is scale, not cost: a full 230-package suite run is hours of CPU and heavy RAM (CI uses --workerIdleMemoryLimit=1300M), though --since / per-workspace scoping makes single-task runs fast.

verified.size_fit: Fails the 20-150 band by ~3x: ~427 curated md in docs/ alone (excluding 285 release notes), ~475 with beps/contrib/root, and ~1,300 more per-package READMEs; ~1,891 md total. Repo is 916MB on checkout with 12,771 commits in 18 months and 230 workspace packages — approaching kubernetes-scale activity, and yarn install alone is a substantial local footprint.
disqualifiers: Docs volume ~3x above the 20-150 md band even after excluding release notes, changelogs, translations, and generated dumps (0 api-report.md dumps found, so the count is genuinely prose)
Giant-class repo: 916MB checkout, 230 workspace packages, ~12.7k commits/18mo — the brief says avoid kubernetes-scale giants, and Backstage's activity volume is in that class
Full test suite and dependency install are heavy in wall-clock/RAM terms, complicating cheap task replay at monorepo scope
verified.summary: Backstage is near-perfect on the top four criteria — genuinely load-bearing prose (ADRs, BEPs, config-schema semantics, STYLE.md conventions all unrecoverable from source), a textbook 230-package yarn monorepo with per-package docs, ~3,660 merged PRs in 18 months with many in the 30-400 line band, and a credential-free Jest suite with SQLite fallbacks — but it decisively fails the size criterion: ~475 curated docs (3x the band) inside a 916MB, giant-class repo the brief explicitly says to avoid, making it a strong but oversized candidate best used only with aggressive scoping to a subset of docs and packages.
